purpose: Compatibility and dependency rules between taxonomy layers. Never says 'impossible' — where a combination is unusual or specialist, flags 'specialist_review_required'. NEX never blocks a customer's design choice on its own authority.
principles: A combination is either COMMON, UNCOMMON (specialist_review_required) or REGIONAL (only common in some markets).
NEX never declares a combination structurally impossible — that judgement belongs to the professional.
Every specialist_review_required combination still submits — it just routes with a flag.

rules.description: A pure glass spiral (all glass, no central column) is not standard.
rules.note: Spirals require a load-bearing central column. All-glass is not a standard construction — treat as a bespoke commission.

rules.description: Paddle / space-saver stairs are legal only as secondary access in most countries.

regional_notes.UK: Approved Doc K limits alternating tread to loft conversion only, single room served
regional_notes.US: IBC 1011.14 restricts alternating tread device to specific uses

rules.description: Standard internal timber species used outdoors will fail quickly.
rules.note: For outdoor stairs use rot-resistant species (Iroko, Teak, Ipê, Accoya) or engineered exterior systems. NEX warns and refers to specialist for species selection.

rules.description: Carpet runner over open-riser stair is unusual but not impossible.
rules.note: Physically possible but visually unusual — runner may look disconnected between treads. Specialist confirms with photos of comparable installs.

rules.description: Horizontal cable balustrades may fail the local 'sphere rule' in residential settings.

regional_thresholds.UK: 100 mm sphere must not pass — horizontal cable typically fails without very tight spacing
regional_thresholds.US: IBC 1015.4 4-inch (~102 mm) sphere rule — horizontal cable often allowed with post spacing engineered
regional_thresholds.AU: NCC — 125 mm sphere rule, cable systems available
regional_thresholds.IT: Italian building code — 100 mm opening rule
regional_thresholds.NL: Bouwbesluit — 100 mm opening rule for residential

rules.description: Frameless structural glass balustrade must be engineered with an appropriate cap and channel.
rules.note: Structural glass balustrade requires engineering calculation — glass thickness, laminate build-up, channel fixing all specialist choices per local glass code (BS 6180, AS 1288, DIN 18008, etc.).

rules.description: Cantilever staircases in pure timber are uncommon — usually stone or steel.
rules.note: Cantilever construction usually uses stone (traditional), reinforced concrete or steel treads with hidden armature. Pure timber cantilever is specialist bespoke.

rules.description: Bolzentreppe (bolt-fixed) is a common form in DACH — rare label elsewhere.
rules.note: In UK/US the same construction is usually marketed as 'floating' or 'wall-mounted' — the customer's region determines which vocabulary the specialist will use.

rules.description: All-glass helical (no visible structure) is a very high-end bespoke commission.
rules.note: All-glass helical requires engineered structural glass system — specialist review always required.

rules.description: Glass stringer (side beam) is uncommon outside curved / helical high-end.
Mono-stringer is most commonly used for straight / quarter turn / half turn geometries.
Stone helical is possible but a very rare high-end commission.
Requesting hidden newels with a solid balustrade needs a top-rail return detail.
rules.note: Solid balustrades usually terminate into newels. Hidden-newel + solid balustrade requires an alternative termination (wall fixing, corner detail) — specialist confirms.

rules.description: Open riser is contemporary in most markets — pairing with traditional turned spindles/newels is unusual visually.
rules.note: Not blocked — but pairing open risers with turned traditional spindles is visually inconsistent. NEX suggests viewing example images before submitting.

rules.description: Some timber species do not take stain evenly.
rules.note: Species like beech and closed-grain pines often blotch when stained. Specialist advises alternative colour approach (dye, tint lacquer).

rules.description: Alternating-tread stairs are almost never accepted for commercial primary access.
rules.note: In every researched country, commercial primary staircases have stricter geometry requirements than residential — paddle/alternating-tread will almost certainly not be code-compliant.

rules.description: Bifurcated / imperial staircases are grand-space features.
rules.note: Bifurcated staircases require substantial floor area. NEX cannot check floor area — specialist confirms with site measurement.

rules.description: Any combination the customer flags as 'special' or 'unusual' routes to specialist without NEX judgement.
rules.note: NEX's default posture: when the customer signals unusualness, trust them and route to specialist.

UK.note: UK residential dominated by timber closed-string L or U-shape.

US.note: Cable balustrade is a distinctly popular US market — much more common than UK.

DE.note: DACH residential includes Bolzentreppe and Faltwerktreppe as mainstream, not niche.

IT.note: Italian residential often has concrete substructure with timber cladding.

ES.note: Spanish residential often concrete substructure with stone/wood tread cladding — very different pricing from all-timber.

NL.note: Dutch homes traditionally use very steep straight stairs — steeper than most other EU countries. Specialist confirms.

BE.note: Belgian market splits Dutch (Flanders) and French (Wallonia) vocabulary — CountryPicker + language toggle both matter.

AU.notable_market: carpet_to_timber_conversion is a huge AU commercial anchor — many existing homes have carpeted timber substructure to be converted to exposed timber.
